transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Start: 14:30 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Alex Murray (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Kwan (CISO, StratusCardio), Marco Ruiz (Lead DevOps), Sonia Patel (Data Privacy), Jared Lee (ML Engineer)

Summary:
Quick intake focused on feasibility of fully air-gapped, on-prem deployment inside a regulated hospital network. Key concerns: offline update mechanism, cryptographic signing of artifacts, hardware constraints (no NVLink for some racks), maintenance windows, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs and evidence for auditors. Next: share checklist + run perf estimates for their node spec.

Topics Covered:
- Deployment modes: private VPC vs physically air-gapped facility
- Update channels: signed images, USB/airdrop, portable bastion, jump box with temporary network egress
- HW constraints: mixed GPU fleet (2xA100 + 4x3090-ish), limited NVLink, no persistent internet to model hub
- Security: HSM/KMS, SAML/SSO, audit logs, data residency, no telemetry allowed
- SLA and rollback: rollback plan for bad updates, canary in lab rack

Transcript Body:
00:00 Alex Murray: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 50 minutes. I'll kick off quick intros and then Priya will walk the infra questions.
00:12 Dr. Elena Kwan: Hi all, Elena here. I run security and compliance for StratusCardio. Quick ask up front—we need no outbound telemetry and full auditability for any package you bring in.
00:24 Alex Murray: 100% understood, Elena. We'll talk through the signed image flow and audit logs.
00:30 Marco Ruiz: Hi. Marco, lead ops. A couple constraints—our machine room is physically isolated, no internet, and the racks are older so NVLink is inconsistent between racks, some are single-socket with consumer GPUs.
00:44 Priya Desai: Thanks Marco. That matters for batching and KV cache. If NVLink isn't present we can't assume cross-GPU sharding without software-based PCIe transfers, which affects latency.
00:56 Jared Lee: Hey, Jared. We're the ML folks. Curious about model pinning—can we pin to a specific compiled variant? We need determinism for validation.
01:06 Priya Desai: Yes, you can pin exact model build IDs. For air-gapped, we'd provide signed artifacts—container images and model blobs—together with a signature file.
01:16 Sonia Patel: Data privacy note—no logs leaving the network. All logging must be customer-managed and removable on demand.
01:25 Alex Murray: Got it. That's common for regulated health. We'll show options: full offline-only mode where console is read-only via exported reports, plus an enterprise agent for local metrics.
01:38 Marco Ruiz: Walk me through the update path. How do we apply patches if there's no network?
01:44 Priya Desai: Two patterns we see: 1) Signed offline bundles that you bring in on encrypted media; or 2) a staging 'bastion' that you connect temporarily from a vetted jump server to pull images, then disconnect. Both require signature verification and local artifact attestation.
02:02 Dr. Elena Kwan: We prefer the pure offline bundle. Our auditors don't like any transient egress even for staging. But we need a deterministic verification step.
02:12 Priya Desai: Then the flow is: Redwood generates a signed bundle, we provide a detached signature (PKI), customer verifies signature with their key or our cert chain, then apply using the Redwood offline installer. Installer writes an immutable, versioned artifact and records local audit entries.
02:33 Marco Ruiz: What's the size of these bundles for a typical medium model—say 7B? We have limited secure media sizes.
02:39 Priya Desai: 7B quantized ~4-6GB depending on format. Full fp16 could be 10-16GB. We can provide delta patches too—only changed layers.
02:51 Jared Lee: Any support for quantization profiles? We run mixed precision and sometimes do INT8/JIT quant.
02:57 Priya Desai: We support pre-quantized artifacts and the runtime has quant-friendly kernels. For strict air-gap you'd import the quantized model artifact. We can recommend a quantization profile based on the exact GPU and perf target.
03:12 Alex Murray: Quick agenda check—after infra we want to align on perf targets and then compliance evidence you need.
03:19 Dr. Elena Kwan: Sounds good.
03:21 Marco Ruiz: Also schedule limitations: we only open racks for updates on Tuesdays 02:00-05:00 local time.
03:29 Alex Murray: Noted. We'll map any update cadence to your windows.
03:35 Priya Desai: On the runtime side—if your fleet mixes consumer cards, we recommend grouping homogeneous racks for serving vs experimentation. NVLink absence pushes more single-node serving with larger batch sizes, which impacts latency.
04:00 Marco Ruiz: Our goal is p95 < 150ms for 512 tokens on day-one, but we're flexible if it's unrealistic.
04:09 Priya Desai: That p95 is aggressive on older consumer GPUs especially without NVLink. We should run a perf estimate—if we target 150ms p95 at 512 tokens, might need 2x A100-equivalent per 10 qps depending on model. We'll run numbers for your exact topology.
04:30 Jared Lee: Do you do continuous KV caching across restarts? If we power cycle a node, does the cache warmup cost hit us?
04:38 Priya Desai: For air-gapped private we support persistent KV cache on local SSD with a warmup/replay flow. You can also snapshot KV to persistent storage and restore after reboot. That requires local disk encrypted at rest—supported.
04:53 Sonia Patel: Encryption requirements—keys must live in our HSM or KMS on-prem. We cannot have Redwood-managed keys.
05:00 Alex Murray: We support customer-managed keys via KMIP-compatible HSMs or on-prem KMS. For the signed bundle flow we can also support your public key for signature verification so private key never leaves your HSM.
05:14 Dr. Elena Kwan: Audit trail—what do you provide as evidence for auditors?
05:18 Priya Desai: We produce a signed installation manifest with checksums, a local audit log of install actions, and can produce a compact evidence package that includes timestamps, checksums, and operator ID. All artefacts stay in your environment.
05:36 Marco Ruiz: How about telemetry—are there any heartbeats or phone home? We need absolute control.
05:42 Alex Murray: For air-gapped customers we can disable phone-home entirely. The console can be run offline; if you want, you can export reports manually. No telemetry unless you opt-in via explicit configuration.
05:55 Jared Lee: For updates, will you provide a signed kernel or image we just dd to a partition? Or is it container-based?
06:03 Priya Desai: Typically we provide signed OCI images plus a signed artifact for the model. The offline installer will verify signatures, unpack to a sealed path and update containerd runtime. For more locked-down environments we can provide a raw signed disk image too.
06:18 Marco Ruiz: Disk image is preferable for some of our isolated devices. Any support for PXE-less provisioning?
06:24 Priya Desai: Yes, we can supply pre-built images or a USB-based installer. The process is flexible; we document checksums, sign, and you can verify via the HSM-backed public key.
06:33 Dr. Elena Kwan: Let's talk about SSO—our operators use SAML. Can the admin console integrate with SAML with no external calls?
06:40 Alex Murray: The console can be configured to use your IdP via SAML metadata exchange. In fully offline cases, you exchange metadata files and configure locally—no external call required after setup.
06:53 Sonia Patel: RBAC granularity—operators should have limited privileges, and ML folks have model validation sandbox.
06:59 Priya Desai: We support RBAC and custom roles; we recommend a least-privilege role for install operators and a separate role for model validators.
07:10 Marco Ruiz: What about rolling back a bad model? If we deploy and see regressions, what's the rollback procedure offline?
07:18 Priya Desai: Installer keeps previous versions and can reinstate last-known-good with a single CLI command. We also support staged canaries on a lab rack so you can validate before wide rollout. The canary flow is fully offline.
07:33 Jared Lee: Do you provide evaluation harnesses we can run locally to assert output quality pre-rollout?
07:38 Priya Desai: Yes, we include an eval runner that can run your test prompts against the pinned model build and produce diff reports. Those are file-based and can be run in your environment.
07:50 Alex Murray: Quick check—are there any showstoppers we haven't covered?
07:54 Dr. Elena Kwan: Two items: proof that keys never leave our HSM, and a signed evidence bundle for each install event for auditors.
08:01 Alex Murray: We can support both. We'll share the crypto flow doc.
08:06 Marco Ruiz: Bandwidth from secure media is low—if a 10GB model arrives on USB we'll be copying it across many nodes. Do you support local registry mirror or peer-to-peer distribution?
08:17 Priya Desai: Yes, offline registry mirror is supported. We also have a secure multicast-style peer distribution we can recommend that verifies checksums per chunk. All signatures validated locally.
08:29 Sonia Patel: Any required ports or services to open?
08:32 Priya Desai: For pure offline, none. For managed monitoring/console you need outbound to specific endpoints. But again, for air-gapped we'll disable telemetry and use manual report export.
08:44 Jared Lee: For ML performance—does Redwood's runtime require vendor-specific drivers? We run some AMD MI250s in other labs.
08:52 Priya Desai: We currently support CUDA-enabled NVIDIA stacks for highest performance. AMD support is on the roadmap but not GA. For MI250 you'd be looking at community runtimes or waiting for our AMD build. We can discuss temporary GPU abstraction layers but performance impacts would be expected.
09:10 Marco Ruiz: That's potentially a blocker, some racks have MI series. We'll compile an inventory.
09:16 Alex Murray: Noted—please include GPU make/model in the asset export.
09:19 Marco Ruiz: Will do.
09:21 Alex Murray: On the contract side, do you anticipate any consumption-based metering inside an air-gapped deployment or is it a flat enterprise license?
09:29 Dr. Elena Kwan: From a procurement perspective, preference for fixed-term appliance license. Metering in an offline environment is messy for audits.
09:36 Alex Murray: We can do a fixed license with optional metering agent that is customer-controlled and stores counters locally; we do not require it to phone home.
09:46 Sonia Patel: Regarding regressions—how do you handle model quality monitoring if we can't share outputs externally?
09:53 Priya Desai: We ship a local quality monitor that runs checks and produces a report bundle you can review. We can also run evaluation hooks pre-rollout as mentioned.
10:06 Jared Lee: Any feature parity difference between hosted Redwood and private air-gapped? Like tool calling, streaming?
10:12 Priya Desai: Most features are supported, but some integrations like managed vector DBs or certain cloud-only autoscaling hooks won't be available. Streaming and function-call style I/O are supported locally.
10:26 Marco Ruiz: Let's talk about acceptance criteria. For us: 1) No telemetry by default, 2) Signed image verification with our key, 3) p95 < 150ms on production 512-token workload, 4) install artifacts and evidence package for auditors. Anything else?
10:44 Alex Murray: That sounds like a solid set. We'll treat that as the acceptance checklist.
10:49 Dr. Elena Kwan: Also add HSM-backed key ownership to that list.
10:52 Alex Murray: Noted.
10:54 Priya Desai: On perf, we'll propose a profile that maps your hardware to expected qps and latency; may need to adjust model size or batching to hit p95.
11:05 Marco Ruiz: Timewise—we want a pilot in Q4. Budget signoff around early September. Any lead time for provisioning?
11:14 Alex Murray: For private air-gapped pilot we typically need 4-6 weeks for packaging, signed artifacts, and a lab canary. If everything aligns you could start testing in late September / early October.
11:25 Dr. Elena Kwan: That timeline could work if we get the compliance docs soon.
11:29 Alex Murray: We'll prioritize sending the compliance + air-gap checklist by Friday.
11:33 Priya Desai: I'll own the perf profile and aim to have an initial estimate by next Wednesday (2026-08-26).
11:40 Marco Ruiz: I'll get the asset list and maintenance windows over by Monday.
11:45 Sonia Patel: I'll validate the evidence format with our audit team and send feedback.
11:50 Alex Murray: Great. Any final questions?
11:54 Dr. Elena Kwan: One more—do you support FIPS-compliant cryptography for the signed bundles?
12:01 Priya Desai: Yes, we can generate FIPS-certified signatures and align to your crypto policy. We'll detail options in the doc.
12:11 Marco Ruiz: That addresses most of it. Thanks.
12:15 Alex Murray: Thanks everyone. Quick recap of next steps: Alex send docs, Priya perf, Marco inventory, Elena compliance gaps. We'll set up the demo/technical runbook session once the inventory is in.
12:31 Alex Murray: I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the technical deep dive and a link to the secure artifact checklist. Expect emails from me and Priya.
12:40 Dr. Elena Kwan: Thanks all.
12:43 Meeting ended.

Post-call Notes:
- Priya flagged AMD GPU limitations—customer has some MI-class hardware; this is a potential risk that could affect the pilot. Action: mark as risk and ask customer to prioritize inventory.
- Confirmed strict no-telemetry requirement and HSM key ownership.
